question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\0 & 1 & 4\\5 & 6 & 0\end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & 1\\3 & 0 & 0\\5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$. (a) Calculate $C = AB - BA$. (b) Prove that $C$ is not a symmetric matrix. (c) Construct a symmetric matrix $D$ using $C$.
explanation:
(a) First calculate $AB$ and $BA$.

$AB = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\\0 & 1 & 4\\5 & 6 & 0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & 1\\3 & 0 & 0\\5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$.

$(AB)_{11} = 1\times2 + 2\times3 + 3\times5 = 23$.

$(AB)_{12} = 1\times0 + 2\times0 + 3\times1 = 3$.

$(AB)_{13} = 1\times1 + 2\times0 + 3\times1 = 4$.

$(AB)_{21} = 0\times2 + 1\times3 + 4\times5 = 23$.

$(AB)_{22} = 0\times0 + 1\times0 + 4\times1 = 4$.

$(AB)_{23} = 0\times1 + 1\times0 + 4\times1 = 4$.

$(AB)_{31} = 5\times2 + 6\times3 + 0\times5 = 28$.

$(AB)_{32} = 5\times0 + 6\times0 + 0\times1 = 0$.

$(AB)_{33} = 5\times1 + 6\times0 + 0\times1 = 5$.

Thus, $AB = \begin{bmatrix}23 & 3 & 4\\23 & 4 & 4\\28 & 0 & 5\end{bmatrix}$.

Now calculate $BA$.

$(BA)_{11} = 7$, $(BA)_{12} = 10$, $(BA)_{13} = 6$.

$(BA)_{21} = 3$, $(BA)_{22} = 6$, $(BA)_{23} = 9$.

$(BA)_{31} = 10$, $(BA)_{32} = 17$, $(BA)_{33} = 19$.

So $BA = \begin{bmatrix}7 & 10 & 6\\3 & 6 & 9\\10 & 17 & 19\end{bmatrix}$.

Now $C = AB - BA = \begin{bmatrix}16 & -7 & -2\\20 & -2 & -5\\18 & -17 & -14\end{bmatrix}$.

(b) To check symmetry compute $C' = \begin{bmatrix}16 & 20 & 18\\-7 & -2 & -17\\-2 & -5 & -14\end{bmatrix}$.

Since $C \neq C'$, $C$ is not symmetric.

(c) A symmetric matrix from $C$ is $D = \frac{1}{2}(C + C')$.

$C + C' = \begin{bmatrix}32 & 13 & 16\\13 & -4 & -22\\16 & -22 & -28\end{bmatrix}$.

$D = \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}32 & 13 & 16\\13 & -4 & -22\\16 & -22 & -28\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}16 & 6.5 & 8\\6.5 & -2 & -11\\8 & -11 & -14\end{bmatrix}$.

This matrix $D$ is symmetric.

options.C:
(a) $C=AB-BA=\begin{bmatrix}16&-7&-2\\20&-2&-5\\18&-17&-14\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Since $C\ne C'$, $C$ is not symmetric.
(c) A symmetric matrix formed from $C$ is $D=\frac12(C+C')=\begin{bmatrix}16&\frac{13}{2}&8\\\frac{13}{2}&-2&-11\\8&-11&-14\end{bmatrix}$.
options.D:
(a) $C=AB+BA$.
(b) $C$ is skew-symmetric because $C'=C$.
(c) A symmetric matrix cannot be constructed from $C$.
